Honestly, I really liked that game - gameplay felt smooth and art direction is absolutely fantastic. I actually liked how these bulky suits of SPEEEHS MEHREENS power armor looked like as well as weaponary.

Still, the story felt quite short IMO and, once again, we have met our common enemy - cliffhanger. By the way, why did they change canonic character from WH40K universe with Titus? Or they are the one, but just have two names? 

I really hope, that one day Space Marine 2 will be released. I'm no fan of tabletop games or books. It were games that introduced me to this savage and bloody universe and it has to be developed further, more independently from outdated designs of GamesWorkshop canons. (cough-cough, Dawn of War 3 I'm talking to you... Damn your hypersex-looking Marines. Dawn of War 2 was way realistic and tactical - exactly how Space Marines gameplay should feel like)

Multiplayer was a failure IMHO - no proper support, paid co-op and lack of diversity.

Anyways, I'd strongly recommend to complete this game, if you're loyal to GOD EMPEROR. Otherwise - you're heretic dog awaiting for exterminatus.

7.5/10
Highly Recomended for any Warhammer 40k fan.

[h1][b]★★★☆☆[/b][/h1]
If I could describe this game in a one word, than that would be 'brown'. Not only because most of the levels are colored brown (despite these being indoors and outdoors), but also because it only seems to be monotonous in its game design (its generic and almost invisible among the hundreds of other brown gameworlds created in the last generation). Ironicly, the orcs also aren't really creative with their words as I heard "Space Marine!" about a hunderd times. 

I'd say this isn't necessarily a bad thing for a game that tries to show of a grim, dark episode of the Warhammer universe, but it does leave a lot to be desired in thematical exploration (not much to learn about the lore here) and gameplay. As for replayability, I'd recommend first time players to start the campaign on Hard, as the first two-thirds of it are a boring slog to play through.

Don't get the game at full price (which is currently 20 bucks). The campaign is only about 6-7 hours long, the multiplayer is basicly dead (daily population around 60 players, as of 2017) and by now there are tons of other action games out there of the same caliber or better. I bought this game because I wanted to explore the lore a bit, but like I wrote above, it doesn't particulairy show that off here.
Too much blood. Not good for mental health.
